subject.title: cron: reject webhook URLs with embedded credentials

question: Should cron reject credential-bearing webhook URLs fail-closed for existing stored jobs, or must this hardening include upgrade-safe doctor/warning behavior before merge?
rationale: Both choices are plausible security policy, but the shared helper affects persisted cron delivery and legacy migration paths, so automation should not choose the upgrade contract on its own.

options.title: Require upgrade-safe hardening
options.body: Add tested migration or redacted warning behavior for stored primary, completion, failure, and legacy webhook targets before enforcing userinfo rejection.

options.title: Accept fail-closed behavior
options.body: Explicitly decide that existing credential-bearing cron webhook jobs should stop delivering until operators move credentials to supported auth mechanisms.

options.title: Pause for a maintainer-owned design
options.body: Close or pause this branch if cron credential URL policy needs a broader security design rather than a helper-only patch.

recommendation.title: Require upgrade-safe hardening
recommendation.body: Add tested migration or redacted warning behavior for stored primary, completion, failure, and legacy webhook targets before enforcing userinfo rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main cron helper and related migration/dispatch lines are attributed to steipete's recent PR 100263 refactor, making him the best available routing owner for the current landing shape.
